text:
Elena (People Ops): Quick help  member had an ambulance pick-up on the Canadian side of Niagara Falls and was transported across the border to a Buffalo ER. Provider is asking for a payment guarantee / direct-bill. Claim 2026-CA-NF-301. Who owns this flow and what docs do we need?

Omar (Benefits): Benefits owns coverage/adjudication. For emergency cross-border ambulance we need: signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB) from the member, EMS run sheet / ambulance itemized invoice, ER admission note showing transfer, provider business license and tax ID, and any vendor billing portal endpoint. We also need the member to confirm it was an emergency (brief statement).

Priya (Finance): Finance handles vendor payment and KYC. We do not issue open "guarantees" but can provide a conditional payment confirmation after claims review and receipt of AOB + KYC. For Canadian payouts we accept CAD wires (account # + transit/institution) or SWIFT for USD/CAD. Provider must supply beneficiary name exactly as bank record and a scanned bank confirmation. Also need a vendor tax form (Canadian equivalent) and remittance contact.

Elena (People Ops): Can someone paste a short provider-facing checklist/email I can forward that explains documents we need and the conditional confirmation language? Provider wants to see a template before sending docs.

Omar (Benefits): Paste below (short):

To: billing@emsclinic.ca
Subject: Redwood Inference  Direct-bill request for patient [MemberName] (Claim 2026-CA-NF-301)

Hello,

Thank you for contacting us. To review a direct payment or provide a conditional payment confirmation, please send the following: 1) Signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB) from the patient (PDF); 2) EMS run sheet and itemized ambulance invoice; 3) ER admission note documenting the transfer; 4) Provider business license and tax ID; 5) Banking details for wire (CAD account + transit/institution OR SWIFT + account), and a bank confirmation showing the account belongs to the clinic; 6) Billing contact name and email.

Please note: we can issue a conditional payment confirmation after we receive and review the above. Final payment requires claims adjudication and may be subject to plan out-of-network rules. Send materials to claims@redwood.com and reference Claim 2026-CA-NF-301.

Priya (Finance): Add small line for currency: "If you prefer USD payout, indicate that and provide SWIFT details; USD wires may require correspondent banks and could add 3-7 business days."

ClaimsBot: Automated: Cross-border emergency claim flagged for manual review. Expected adjudication 5-12 business days after complete docs received.

Elena (People Ops): Thanks  I'll forward this to the clinic. One last Q: clinic asked if we can send the member-facing EOB with initials only (no full name) when we email the patient. Is that allowed?

Omar (Benefits): Member-facing formatting follows member preference. We can send initials-only if the member signs a consent allowing that. Internally we must retain full name and full EOB for audit. Any suppression requires written consent recorded in the claim.

Priya (Finance): Also flag: if the provider requests a conditional confirmation letter, have them include an invoice estimate; AP will only sign a confirmation that is explicit about conditionality and subject to final adjudication.

Elena (People Ops): Great, forwarding now and will update the thread when they reply. :thumbsup: (end of thread)
